title: Flat lower opcycle of a bounded flat derived approximation
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small relative to the universe of its module sheaves, with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use $D(\mathcal O)$ and its cohomology functors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and the derived tensor product computed by K-flat resolutions and total tensor complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $a\le b$ be integers. Let $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ satisfy $H^j(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}N)=0$ for every module sheaf $N$ in degree zero and every $j\notin[a,b]$. Let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded cochain complex of module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and $P^j=0$ for $j<a-1$. Suppose there is a morphism $f:P^\bullet\to K$ in $D(\mathcal O)$ such that $H^j(f)$ is an isomorphism for every $j\ge a$. Then the cokernel sheaf $Q=\operatorname{coker}(d_P^{a-1}:P^{a-1}\to P^a)$ is flat. No finiteness or local projectivity of the terms of $P^\bullet$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08G7 (lemma-perfect-precise), proof: cone construction through flatness of E′, before the finite-presentation/local-summand argument. The same argument only requires bounded flat approximation terms.

proof.text: First $H^j(K)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. Indeed choose a flat-term K-flat representative $L$ of $K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The comparison [lem-sf-ringed-kflat-single-tensor-comparison] for $M=\mathcal O$ computes $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O$ by $L\otimes\mathcal O$. The unit maps $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$ and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ identify this complex with $L$, by the tensor unit in [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. Apply the hypothesis to $N=\mathcal O$.

source.place: Tag 08G7, lemma-perfect-precise: vanishing of cohomology of E; Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor

proof.text: Put $Z=\ker(d_P^{a-1})$. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] to $Z[0]$ with upper bound zero. Obtain a flat complex $F$ with $F^i=0$ for $i>0$ and an epimorphic quasi-isomorphism $\epsilon:F\to Z[0]$. Thus $\cdots\to F^{-1}\to F^0\xrightarrow{\epsilon^0}Z\to0$ is exact. Form $E$ by setting $E^j=P^j$ for $j\ge a-1$ and $E^j=F^{j-a+2}$ for $j\le a-2$. The differential $E^{a-2}\to E^{a-1}$ is $F^0\xrightarrow{\epsilon^0}Z\hookrightarrow P^{a-1}$; all other differentials are those of $F$ or $P$. The two new adjacent composites vanish since $\epsilon^0d_F^{-1}=0$ and $d_P^{a-1}|_Z=0$. Every term is flat and $E$ is bounded above. This explicitly resolves the kernel that occurs in the cone calculation of Tag 08G7.

source.place: Tag 08G7, lemma-perfect-precise: kernel K in the cone; Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution, bounded-above flat-resolution construction

proof.text: Let $T=\tau_{\ge a}P$ as in [def-kun-truncations]: $T^a=\operatorname{coker}d_P^{a-1}$ and $T^j=P^j$ for $j>a$. Define $e:E\to T$ by the quotient $P^a\to T^a$ in degree $a$, identity above $a$, and zero below $a$. Its chain-map equation at $a-1$ is the cokernel identity $q d_P^{a-1}=0$. Exactness of the augmented resolution gives $H^j(E)=0$ for $j\le a-2$; at $a-1$ the incoming image is $Z=\ker d_P^{a-1}$, so this cohomology is also zero. In degree $a$, the kernel of the induced $Q\to P^{a+1}$ is $(\ker d_P^a)/\operatorname{im}d_P^{a-1}$; above $a$ the cohomology is unchanged. Thus $e$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $Q(E)\cong Q(T)$.

source.place: Tag 08G7, lemma-perfect-precise: resolve the single kernel in degree a-1; explicit cohomology computation

proof.text: Functorial truncation gives $\tau_{\ge a}f:Q(T)\to\tau_{\ge a}K$. The truncation functors and their natural units are those of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](1); [def-kun-truncations] gives their retained cohomology. For $j\ge a$ this map induces $H^j(f)$ under the natural truncation identifications, hence an isomorphism; below $a$ both sides vanish. Also the unit $K\to\tau_{\ge a}K$ is an isomorphism on all cohomology by step 1. All these objects lie in the strictly full $D^+$ of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] to these two maps. Together with $Q(e)$ from step 3 this gives an isomorphism $g:Q(E)\cong K$, without representing $f$ by a chain map.

source.place: Tag 08G7, lemma-perfect-precise: removing the lone lower kernel; derived.tex Tag 05RU, bounded-below full subcategory and cohomology detection

proof.text: Since $E$ is bounded above with flat terms, [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] makes it K-flat. For every module sheaf $N$, [lem-sf-ringed-kflat-single-tensor-comparison] identifies $Q(E)\otimes^{\mathbf L}N$ with $Q(E\otimes N)$. Tensoring the isomorphism $g$ identifies the former with $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}N$. Consequently $H^{a-1}(E\otimes N)=0$ by the Tor-amplitude hypothesis. The symmetry of sheaf tensor in [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] identifies this with $H^{a-1}(N\otimes E)=0$; with $N$ in degree zero its total differential is $1_N\otimes d_E$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-opcycles-tor-criterion] to $E$ and $n=a$, using its flat terms and the universal exactness established in step 5. Its conclusion is that $\operatorname{coker}(d_E^{a-1})$ is flat. But $E^{a-1}=P^{a-1}$, $E^a=P^a$, and $d_E^{a-1}=d_P^{a-1}$ by construction. Its cokernel is therefore exactly the sheaf $Q$ in the statement, giving the conclusion without any finite-generation assumption.

source.place: Tag 08G7 (lemma-perfect-precise), flatness of E′; Tag 08G0 (lemma-last-one-flat), universal-tensor criterion

lean.statement: theorem isFlatOnSite_cokernel_of_bounded_flat_approximation {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [EssentiallySmall.{r} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{r}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{r} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R))] (a b : ℤ) (_hab : a ≤ b) (K : DerivedCategory (ringedSiteModules.{r} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R))) (_hTor : ∀ (N : ringedSiteModules.{r} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R)) (j : ℤ), j < a ∨ b < j → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ j).obj ((siteDerivedTensorIndependentCoefficients J R).obj (K, (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj N)))) (P : CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{r} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R)) ℤ) (_hbounded : ∃ l n : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, j < l ∨ n < j → IsZero (P.X j)) (_hflat : ∀ j : ℤ, IsFlatOnSite (J := J) (R := R) (P.X j)) (_hzero : ∀ j : ℤ, j < a - 1 → IsZero (P.X j)) (f : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ⟶ K) (_hf : ∀ j : ℤ, a ≤ j → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ j).map f)) : IsFlatOnSite (J := J) (R := R) (cokernel (P.d (a - 1) a))
